ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Marcus Aurelius — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. Aurelius is a 53-year-old man with reflux esophagitis diagnosed ten weeks ago, on omeprazole, chronic insomnia in cognitive behavioral therapy, and long-standing use of an opium-containing herbal paste, who comes for the preventive visit booked at intake. The COVID-19 illness three weeks ago settled in five days without antiviral treatment; the cough has gone and his energy is back. He took no extra remedy while ill and used no cough syrup. He finished the eight-week omeprazole course two weeks ago and has taken it on demand twice since, each time after a late dinner; otherwise he has no reflux symptoms, and he eats his main meal earlier. He has taken the paste on alternate nights since early June; he has decided that from tonight he will take a smaller amount on only two nights a week. He has never had colorectal cancer screening or a pneumococcal or shingles vaccine. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 0174-07-28; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 64.4 kg, BMI 21.8; blood pressure 118/76, pulse 70

Burning and pressing pain in the upper abdomen and lower chest after meals, for more than a year and worse over three months, with poor appetite, waking at night with pain and a sour taste, and a 3 kg weight loss; not brought on by exertion; normal ECG; cardiac and peptic causes to be excluded
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis at endoscopy; its pattern echoes the stomach and chest complaints and the pain with food that Dio describes (D).

Gastroesophageal reflux disease with erosive esophagitis, Los Angeles grade B, and a 2 cm sliding hiatal hernia; Helicobacter pylori negative on biopsy; coronary disease excluded by CT coronary angiography; synthetic modern diagnosis for his documented stomach and chest complaints
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the cause of his real complaints is unknown and no historical diagnosis is made.

Daily use of an unregulated opium-containing herbal remedy for about six years, for stomach pain and sleep; opioid use disorder criteria not met (one DSM-5-TR criterion, restlessness and poor sleep when he stopped it); expected physiological dependence; constipation and possibly slowed gastric emptying from the opioid

Follow-up: Fifteen-week review as planned, with PHQ-9, GAD-7, the Insomnia Severity Index and the second hepatitis B dose. HIV and hepatitis results by phone. Colonoscopy as ordered. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 0174-08-25: fifteen-week review after the eight-week omeprazole course: on-demand therapy, sleep, the remedy, and mood. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He wants full treatment for any condition from which he could recover to his present life and work, and does not want his life prolonged by machines if he could not. He named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and will write his wishes down in his own words. To be revisited yearly. [S]
